subject: Private footprint transition and segmentation request
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@medwell.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private footprint transition and segmentation request

Hi Rachel —

Happy Friday. As we approach your annual renewal window (2026-10-01), I wanted to surface the options we discussed in our last QBR for migrating your core inference traffic to a segmented private footprint. High-level items MedWell asked for: an additional isolated analytics cluster, a new edge environment in us-west for latency-sensitive telemetry, and a 12->24 month term adjustment to align with your internal budgeting cadence.

Attached is a preliminary SOW and a simple segmentation diagram showing the proposed topology. Ask: can you confirm MedWell’s procurement/ops timeline for approving a scope change so we can reserve dedicated nodes and coordinate a soft cutover window?

Next steps I propose:
- Your confirmation of target go-live (we recommend 2026-11-15 for a phased rollout)
- Procurement headcount and PO lead so we can draft the amendment
- Any additional isolation controls (HSM/KMS, audit retention beyond default) we should include in the SOW

I’m looping in Marcus and Dev for sizing & ops questions.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments referenced: Redwood_SOW_MedWell_v2.pdf; segmentation-topology-2026-08.drawio.png
From: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@medwell.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: MedWell Procurement <procurement@medwell.com>, MedWell Ops <ops@medwell.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private footprint transition and segmentation request

Neha —

Thanks for the note and the SOW. A few clarifications from procurement/ops on our side:

1) Term: We prefer a 24-month committed term but need the option to add a 30-day performance window post-cutover before true billing ramps (to validate isolated analytics ingestion). Is that feasible?
2) Cost: Please provide a line-item break for the new edge nodes and the isolated analytics cluster separately — procurement wants clear OPEX vs CAPEX mapping for their internal cost model.
3) Security: We do require KMS integration with our vault, plus an audit log retention uplift to 3 years for the analytics cluster.

Timeline: procurement will review vendor amendments 2026-09-10 and aims to issue an initial PO by 2026-09-20 if terms align. Ops will need a dry-run week for the cutover in the staging environment.

Can your team update the SOW and provide a revised cost breakdown by next Wednesday (2026-09-01)?

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Lee
Director, Cloud Purchasing — MedWell Health

On Fri, Aug 29, 2026 at 09:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@medwell.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private footprint transition and segmentation request

Hi Rachel — quick technical response to the security and dry-run asks.

- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and on-prem HSM gateways. For MedWell’s vault integration we’ll need a service principal and a short configuration window (approx 2 business days) to validate key rotations in staging.
- Audit logs: We can extend retention to 3 years for the analytics cluster. Note this increases storage costs — I’ll include a delta estimate.
- Dry-run: We recommend a 3-day staging dry-run (not just a single week) to exercise prefix caching and routing fallbacks. We can provision a temporary staging env that mirrors production for the cutover rehearsal.

I’ll produce a technical appendix for the SOW covering required access, test accounts, and the dry-run checklist. Marcus — can you confirm node sizing for the analytics cluster based on current ingestion rates?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

> On Aug 29, 2026, at 11:03 AM, Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@medwell.com> wrote:
> > (procurement questions)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@medwell.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private footprint transition and segmentation request

Rachel —

Sizing notes: based on MedWell’s current token throughput and the analytics retention profile you shared, recommended baseline for the isolated analytics cluster is: 4x A100-equivalent nodes with 48GB KV caches and a burst pool of 2 additional nodes for peak ETL windows. Edge environment in us-west: 3x T4-equivalent nodes to keep sub-30ms p99 for telemetry reads.

Cost delta: I’ll publish a line-item estimate in the revised SOW, but ballpark monthly uplift for the analytics cluster + edge environment (including 3-year audit retention) is ~$28k/mo on top of existing committed capacity. We can discuss committed discounts tied to a 24-month term.

I agree with Dev that a 3-day staging dry-run is the right move — we’ll include a dry-run runbook and rollback playbook.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Lee <rachel.lee@medwell.com>, MedWell Procurement <procurement@medwell.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T16:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private footprint transition and segmentation request — next steps and updated SOW

Rachel / team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is the updated SOW and the cost breakdown (see attachments). Key callouts in this revision:

- Term: redwood can support a 24-month committed term with a 30-day performance validation window post-cutover where MedWell pays the prior committed rate and we run joint verification checks.
- Line-item pricing: analytics cluster and edge environment are broken out with one-time provisioning fees and monthly committed/usage tiers.
- Security: KMS integration appendix and 3-year audit retention added.
- Dry-run: scheduling options for a 3-day staging rehearsal in the week of 2026-11-01; suggested cutover target remains 2026-11-15.

Next steps:
1) Procurement review and feedback by 2026-09-10 (we captured your timeline).
2) If acceptable, upload the PO and request countersignature via DocuSign — I included a placeholder envelope link in the related links.
3) Ops and dev to schedule a 2-hour kickoff tech call to confirm staging credentials. Grace from our contracts team is copied to expedite the amendment and discount approval.

If procurement wants a tighter SLA or additional fallbacks during the 30-day validation period Grace can confirm discount/cost tradeoffs.

Appreciate the partnership — let us know if you'd like a short call tomorrow to walk the SOW line-by-line.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
